Tread blocks look deep with visible pattern; no obvious sidewall bulge is visible in these angles.
Photo 2 shows the brand/model text on the tire sidewall: 'MAXXIS' is readable.
No clear tire size (e.g., 195/65R15) is readable in the provided photos.
No clear evidence of patching is visible, but the photos do not show the full sidewall/inner area where repairs are usually seen.

Photos suggest good tread depth, but no tread-depth measurement (mm) is shown.

risks.risk: Tire size is not readable; wrong size can make the price unusable for the buyer.
risks.proof: A clear photo of the full sidewall showing the full size marking (e.g., 195/65R15) and load/speed rating.
risks.if_unproven: Priced at worst-case for unknown size/fit risk (buyer should treat as not confirmed for their vehicle).

risks.risk: DOT date (age) not shown; older tires can fail sooner even if tread looks good.
risks.proof: A close-up photo of the DOT code on the sidewall (week/year).
risks.if_unproven: Priced as older/unknown age (worst-case: reduced lifespan).

risks.risk: No patch/bulge not fully verifiable; hidden repairs or internal damage may exist.
risks.proof: Photos of the entire tire circumference (both sidewalls and tread) plus a close-up of any suspicious spots; ideally a photo of the inside bead area.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as potentially repaired/unknown condition (worst-case: treat as not guaranteed).

risks.risk: Quantity/fitment not fully confirmed (photos show at least 2 tires, but not explicitly confirmed).
risks.proof: Confirm how many tires are included and whether they are the same size and same tread pattern.
risks.if_unproven: Priced assuming the worst-case quantity/consistency (buyer should confirm before paying).

proof_requests: Clear sidewall close-up showing the full tire size (e.g., 195/65R15) and load/speed rating.
Close-up of the DOT date code (week/year) for each tire.
Full 360° photos of each tire: both sidewalls and the entire tread surface (no cropping).
Confirm the exact number of tires included and whether both are the same size/model.
response.reason: The photos confirm Maxxis tires with good-looking tread, but the key pricing drivers (exact size and DOT age) are not readable, and 'no patch/no bulge' and '90% tread' are not measurable from these angles. Request the sidewall size and DOT code first.
